issues.description: The solution's PersonService has a different constructor signature / initialization than the template. The template provides constructor-based injection (public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository)) and a non-null final personRepository field, whereas the solution declares a no-argument constructor that sets the final personRepository to null. This is a structural contradiction: it prevents normal constructor injection and would cause runtime null-pointer failures when methods call personRepository. It also conflicts with the template's and typical Spring usage, confusing students about how PersonRepository is supposed to be injected and used.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution's PersonService match the template's constructor-based injection. Restore a constructor that accepts PersonRepository (e.g., public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository) { this.personRepository = personRepository; }) or otherwise ensure Spring injects the repository (for example, use @Autowired on a non-final field or on a constructor). Do not set the final repository field to null. This preserves the intended dependency injection design and avoids runtime null-pointer errors.
